fields.meta_title: Church Survey Template and Questions | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a church survey members can answer on paper or by phone, with no names attached and results each ministry leader can act on.
fields.h1: Build a Church Survey Your Congregation Will Answer
fields.hero_description: Build a church survey that members answer on a phone or a paper card, with no names collected and results sorted by ministry.
fields.features_heading: Made for the Way a Congregation Answers
fields.features_subheading: Each piece covers a real Sunday: phones in the seats, cards in the pews, and leaders who need their own numbers.
fields.feature_1:
Anonymous answers with a group minimum

Leave name and email off the survey and say so on the first screen. Reports hold back any group smaller than 5, which keeps a class of six from being read person by person.
fields.feature_2:
Paper cards typed in by volunteers

Print the questions on a card for members who prefer to write. Volunteers enter each card on a short screen, and those answers sit beside the phone answers, marked as paper.
fields.feature_3:
Ministry questions only for those involved

Ask parents about the kids' program and skip that page for everyone else. Each ministry section opens only for people who say they take part, which keeps the survey short.
fields.feature_4:
A guest card that asks before calling

Print a QR code on the card first-time guests fill in and keep it to a handful of questions. Anyone who asks for a call goes on a list emailed to the welcome team lead.
fields.feature_5:
Results each ministry leader can read

Give the youth leader the youth answers and the groups director the groups table. The leadership team sees the whole survey, and every chart compares this year with last year.
fields.feature_6:
Every answer in a database you own

Keep each response as a row in your own database, with no cap on how many come in. Export the full survey app to your GitHub repository on paid plans and keep changing it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Church Surveys in the Field
fields.tab_content_1:
Paper cards and phones, counted as one

Alder Street Church runs its congregation survey for three weeks each fall. Members answer on their phones through a QR code in the bulletin, or on a paper card that volunteers type in after the service. This year 318 people answered, 77 of them on paper. An age group with fewer than 5 answers stays out of the report.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every first-time guest on a Monday list

Guests at Copper Ridge scan a QR code on the welcome card and answer four questions, ending with whether they would like a call. Last Sunday 9 guests filled it in. At 8 a.m. Monday, Nora Whitfield, who leads the welcome team, got an email naming the 3 who said yes.
fields.tab_content_3:
What 164 members asked for after the season

Linden Hall ends each 10-week small group season with a short survey. Leaders see their own group, and only once 5 members have replied. This fall 164 members answered across 22 groups. Childcare during the meeting topped the requests at 58, and the groups director has the full table.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which start time 205 households would pick

Sparrow Hill is weighing a second Sunday service and asked every household which start time it would attend. In two weeks, 205 households answered: 118 chose 9:00 and 87 chose 11:15. Households with children leaned to 9:00 by 61 to 23. The leadership team read the split before setting a date.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Church Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a church survey members will finish and trust, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the results will change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep it short enough to finish
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write questions that do not lead
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decisions the answers should inform before writing any question, such as service times or how the church shares news. A survey with nothing riding on it spends the congregation's goodwill and gives the staff nothing to act on.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Aim for a survey people can finish in about 7 minutes on a phone, and time it on a volunteer before it goes out. Completion drops once surveys run longer, and the open questions near the end are often the ones staff most want answered.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask about one thing per question and keep the wording neutral. A question that praises the program before asking for a rating pushes people toward a kind answer. Offer a balanced scale, and add a skip option for questions that may not apply.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Say on the first screen that no names are collected, and leave out name and email fields. Set a reporting minimum of 5 for every group. Age bands and ministry areas should be broad enough that nobody can be picked out.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Offer paper next to the QR code
fields.howto_step_5_des: Print the same questions on a card and leave a stack in the seats. Some members will never open a link, and a card reaches them. Ask two volunteers to type the cards in each week while the survey stays open.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Keep a handful of questions word for word every year, in the same order, and add new ones after them. Only identical wording lets you say belonging went up or down. Field the survey in the same month each year as well.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the results with ministry leads
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sit down with the people who run each ministry and go through their section first. Then share a short summary with the congregation, with one or two changes the church will make, before the next survey opens.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a church survey for my congregation that keeps every answer anonymous and shows results for each ministry.

plan.angle: The top 10 are question lists and downloadable templates (LimeSurvey, SurveyLegend, Jotform, Tithely, Vanco), a congregational-study service (Hartford Institute, Barna) and a pastors' thread asking whether a survey is worth running. None shows a church survey once it is in the field: answers that arrive on paper and on phones and must be counted together, a guest card that has to reach the welcome team by Monday, a groups season whose feedback should change next term, and a decision the leadership team wants the congregation's view on first. This page answers the question-list intent in the FAQ and how-to, then shows those four surveys running, with anonymity rules a church can state up front and results routed to the person who acts on them.

claims_to_source: Survey reports commonly hide any group with fewer than 5 responses so no one can be identified
Longer surveys see more people quit before the end, so shorter surveys get more complete responses
Leading or loaded wording biases answers, so survey questions should be neutral
Offering a paper version alongside an online one reaches people who would not answer online
Asking the same core questions in the same way each time is what makes results comparable across rounds
